review_scope: Full index Chinese–English read: title, five introductory paragraphs, both group headings/notes, all sixteen card titles/decks, both source notes. Ten source-bound local repairs recorded. This is a first alignment audit, not an independent second review.

changes.before: War is the thing the Kingdom of Ends must handle and least wants to happen. Staying silent about it hands the whole field over to other discourses. And once you do speak, one thing has to be settled first: the protagonist of this series is not war but cultivation — the process by which subjectivity deepens and grows into other subjectivity over time. War sits very low on that map. It is the backstop invoked only when cultivation has been broken.
changes.after: War is the thing the Kingdom of Ends must handle and least wants to happen. Staying silent about it hands the whole field over to other discourses. And once you do speak, one thing has to be settled first: the protagonist of this series is not war but cultivation — the process by which subjectivity continually deepens and grows through mutual exchange over time. War sits very low on that map. It is the backstop invoked only when cultivation has been broken.
changes.reason: Restore ongoing mutual growth without implying fusion of subjectivities.

changes.before: The main sequence treats only the 15DD side. This group lets the other side speak: it reads historical works of war philosophy one by one and asks where they run alongside SAE, where they diverge, where they must be criticised, and where SAE has nothing to say. Four working rules govern every volume, and the volumes are ordered by thickness of interface, not by rank.
changes.after: The main sequence treats only the 15DD side. This group lets the other side speak: it reads historical works of war philosophy one by one and asks where they run alongside SAE, where they diverge, where they must be criticised, and where SAE has nothing to say. Four working rules govern every volume: where there is agreement, explain why; where there is disagreement, state SAE's own position rather than correct the other party; where a text touches the ground, criticism is required; where the question lies outside SAE's scope, say nothing. The volumes are ordered by thickness of interface, not by rank.
changes.reason: Restore all four explicitly enumerated working rules, not merely the statement that there are four.

changes.before: Open play draws its force from structural position rather than an information gap, so time is on its side. Deceit's crux is not fooling the enemy but concealing from one's own — and that locks down the entire upward sequence.
changes.after: Open play draws its force from an asymmetry of structural position rather than an information gap, so time is on its side. Deceit's crux is not fooling the enemy but concealing from one's own — and that locks down the entire upward sequence.
changes.reason: Restore 结构位势差 rather than structural position alone. Canonical wording matches the article metadata review.

changes.before: Finish, then step aside, and hand attention back to cultivation. A civilization that walks the sequence to its end grows quieter, not louder — so the silence of the universe asks not where they are, but where we are.
changes.after: Finish, then step aside, and hand attention back to cultivation. A civilization that walks the sequence to its end becomes more hidden, not more conspicuous — so the silence of the universe asks not where they are, but where we are.
changes.reason: Restore visibility, not sound, in the civilization claim. Canonical wording matches the article metadata review.

changes.before: Kant and SAE share a ground and give contrary provisions on whether a defeated state may be made to change its constitution. The same ground does not automatically yield the same line.
changes.after: Kant and SAE share a ground and give contrary provisions on whether a defeated state may be made to change its constitution. The same ground does not automatically yield the same line. Between that ground and any specific line lies a further stretch of reasoning.
changes.reason: Restore the final sentence about the argument still required. Canonical wording matches the article metadata review.

changes.before: Clausewitz and On Protracted War share one form of constraint: war is authorised by an external political purpose and constrained by it. And that form cannot restrain the authoriser itself.
changes.after: Clausewitz and On Protracted War share one form of constraint: war is authorised by an external political purpose and constrained by it. And that form cannot restrain the authoriser itself. The purpose may expand on its own in the course of the war.
changes.reason: Restore the specific mechanism by which the purpose escapes its own constraint. Canonical deck wording; existing emphasis retained.

changes.before: Laozi, the Sima Fa, the Mozi and SAE all refuse to treat war as an ordinary policy option — and their four gates are of four different kinds: attitude, purpose, norm, structure.
changes.after: Laozi, the Sima Fa, the Mozi and SAE all refuse to treat war as an ordinary policy option — and their four gates are of four different kinds: attitude, purpose, norm, structure. The four do not all share the condition that every other road is exhausted.
changes.reason: Restore the decisive final sentence denying a shared last-resort condition. Canonical deck wording; existing emphasis retained.

changes.before: The four theorems are most easily read as a new just war theory. This volume exists to prevent that misreading: SAE does not establish the adjudicating position — and Grotius stands on the same side.
changes.after: The four theorems are most easily read as a new just war theory. This volume exists to prevent that misreading: SAE does not establish the position from which to determine who is the just party — and Grotius stands on the same side.
changes.reason: Restore the specific object of the adjudication in the deck. Canonical wording matches the article metadata review.

changes.before: Sunzi's caution and Theorem One overlap in conclusion, and the two criteria ask after different objects: one after the properties of the prospective war, the other after the state of the relation before it begins.
changes.after: Sunzi's caution and Theorem One overlap in conclusion, and the two criteria ask after different objects: one after the properties of the prospective war, the other after the state of the relation before it begins. Technological progress can therefore loosen the former criterion, but not the latter.
changes.reason: Restore the deck’s final comparison and its direction. Canonical wording matches the article metadata review.

changes.before: Gandhi and SAE are structurally joined at one point: both refuse to reduce the other party to a disposable thing. The disagreement is not whether to act but where each criterion's trigger variables sit.
changes.after: Gandhi and SAE are structurally joined at one point: both refuse to reduce the other party to a disposable thing. The disagreement is not whether to act but where each criterion's trigger variables sit. One points toward the practitioners on one’s own side, the other toward the channels between the two parties.
changes.reason: Restore the deck’s explicit contrast between own practitioners and relational channels. Canonical wording matches the article metadata review.

changes.before: A war completes outside itself. Real losing is breaking your own civilization's cultivation along the way — so a war can be won militarily and lost structurally. Not fighting is also preparing: deepening cultivation in peacetime is the best preparation there is.
changes.after: A war always completes outside itself. Real losing is breaking your own civilization's cultivation along the way — so a war can be won militarily and lost structurally. Not fighting is also preparing: deepening cultivation in peacetime is the best preparation there is.
changes.reason: Restore 永远 in the deck. Canonical wording matches the article metadata review.

changes.before: A victor's two obligations and the firewall against liberating on someone's behalf; why defeat is not losing and self-annihilation is never structurally adequate; and the hidden toxicity of stalemate — you never lost on the battlefield, but across the standoff you became their mirror.
changes.after: A victor's two obligations and the firewall against liberating on someone's behalf; why defeat is not losing and self-annihilation is never structurally adequate; and the most hidden toxicity in a balance of power — you never lost on the battlefield, but across the standoff you became their mirror.
changes.reason: Restore 均势 and its superlative rather than equate it with stalemate. Canonical wording matches the article metadata review.

metadata_reconciliation: All ten reviewed English card-deck amendments use exactly the wording of their per-article metadata receipts; the remaining two changes are the series introduction and group note.
